title: How to Prepare a 3D Modeling Project Before Hiring
h1: How to prepare a 3D modeling project before hiring
description: What a 3D artist needs: purpose of the model, references and measurements, level of detail, materials, file formats, polygon limits and usage rights.
intro: 3D models are used for product images, games, animation, augmented reality, architecture and 3D printing. Each use needs a different kind of model, and a model built for one purpose often fails in another. A detailed product render model may be far too heavy for a mobile game, and a game model may not be accurate enough for manufacturing. This article explains what to decide and prepare before hiring a 3D artist so you get a model that fits its purpose.

faq.a: The number of small surfaces that make up a model. Games and AR need low counts; still renders can use more.

faq.q: Which file format should I ask for?
faq.a: It depends on your software and use. Common formats include FBX, OBJ, GLB and STEP for engineering.

faq.q: Can a 3D model be used for 3D printing?
faq.a: Only if it is built as a closed, printable solid at the right scale. Say so in advance.
Images and material settings that give a model its color, surface detail and finish.
Agree in writing on ownership or license, and ask for the source files.
